title: Magellan and Elcano round the world, 1519–22
summary: Five ships left Sanlúcar for the Spice Islands by the west. Magellan found the strait at the foot of South America and was killed in the Philippines; one ship, the Victoria, came home under Elcano, the first to sail round the world.

events.label: Puerto San Julián: the Easter mutiny
events.text: Wintering on the Patagonian coast on short rations, three of the Spanish captains rose against their Portuguese commander. Magellan took the ships back by a ruse: Mendoza was stabbed in his cabin, Quesada beheaded and quartered, and Cartagena with a priest left ashore when the fleet sailed on.

events.label: Guam: first land after the Pacific
events.text: More than three months from the strait, starving and scurvied, with the crew eating leather and rats, the ships made Guam. The Chamorro came out in outrigger canoes and took what they could, a ship's boat among it; Magellan called the islands the Isles of Thieves and had houses burned and seven Chamorro killed over the boat. They were the first people the fleet had met since South America.

events.label: Cebu: the banquet massacre
events.text: Four days after Magellan fell at Mactan, Rajah Humabon of Cebu, lately baptised, invited the officers ashore to a feast. Some twenty-seven were killed at it, Duarte Barbosa among them; João Serrão was last seen on the beach, begging the ships to ransom him, as they weighed anchor and left him.

events.label: Tidore: the Victoria loads cloves
events.text: Magellan was dead, the fleet reduced to two ships, and Elcano and the remains of the crew found the Spice Islands at last. The Sultan of Tidore sold them cloves enough to pay for the whole expedition. The Victoria sailed home alone; eighteen of the men who had set out came into Sanlúcar.
